name: root-long-help
stdout:
Vyane assembles configured providers, protocols, CLI harnesses, the dispatch kernel, and local storage into one command-line tool.

Usage: vyane [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  check      Validate configuration and show local readiness
  dispatch   Run one task against a profile, provider/model, or auto-routed target
  broadcast  Run one task against several targets concurrently
  history    Show recent run ledger records
  sessions   List saved session records
  session    Inspect and safely reset local continuity sessions
  workflow   Run, resume, and list declarative workflows
  review     Run a built-in multi-model review pipeline (implement → review → synthesize)
  route      Show what the router would pick for a task (dry-run, no dispatch)
  task       Inspect and manage detached background runs
  serve      Start the bearer-authenticated loopback HTTP API server
  daemon     Run and control the authenticated local workflow daemon
  a2a        Use a local SQLite inbox; this is not authenticated A2A protocol transport
  goal       Create, inspect, and advance owner-scoped local goals
  mcp        Run the MCP server over stdio (for use as an MCP tool server)
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --config <PATH>
          Config file to load instead of the default user + project files

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

name: dispatch-help
stdout:
Run one task against a profile, provider/model, or auto-routed target

Usage: vyane dispatch [OPTIONS] --target <TARGET> <TASK>

Arguments:
  <TASK>  Task text to submit

Options:
      --config <PATH>      Config file to load instead of the default user + project files
      --target <TARGET>    Target profile, provider/model pair, or `auto`. Use `profile:auto` to select a profile literally named `auto`
      --workdir <PATH>     Working directory for harness runs
      --sandbox <SANDBOX>  Workspace permission level for harness runs [default: read-only] [possible values: read-only, write, full]
      --session <ID>       Continue or create a logical session id
      --system <TEXT>      System prompt for direct HTTP, appended instructions for harnesses
      --timeout <SECS>     Attempt timeout in seconds; absent means no timeout
      --label <k=v>        Label to store on the run record; repeatable as key=value. Router output fields such as routing.provider and routing.effort are reserved
      --no-frontier        For `--target auto`, prohibit frontier-tier routing
      --detach             Run in the background: spawn a detached worker, print its id, and exit without waiting. Inspect it later with `vyane task`
      --json               Emit machine-readable JSON
      --stream             Stream deltas to stdout as they arrive for one direct-HTTP or CLI-harness target; falls back to non-streaming for sessions or failover chains
  -h, --help               Print help

name: goal-help
stdout:
Create, inspect, and advance owner-scoped local goals

Usage: vyane goal [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  create              Create a queued goal
  get                 Show one goal and its append-only events
  list                List goals by priority and recent activity
  next                Show the highest-priority queued goal
  start               Move a queued or paused goal to in_progress
  claim               Atomically claim a queued goal for a worker under a lease
  claim-next          Atomically select and claim the highest-priority queued goal
  renew               Heartbeat: extend the lease currently held by a worker
  reclaim             Take over a goal whose lease has expired
  satisfy             Record that an acceptance criterion was actually verified
  verify              Run bounded local acceptance checks and persist successful criteria
  pursue              Repeatedly verify and dispatch fresh bounded work segments until achieved or paused
  continuity-next     Project the current continuity next action without mutating or dispatching
  continuity-queue    Queue one approval bound to the current ready takeover or review step; never dispatches
  continuity-decide   Explicitly approve or reject one pending continuity approval
  continuity-execute  Consume one approved continuity approval and execute exactly once
  continuity-signal   Record one exact external continuity readiness signal; never dispatches
  progress            Append a progress event without changing lifecycle state
  pause               Pause an in-progress goal; releases any lease (holder-only while leased)
  resume              Resume a paused goal; resumed goals are always unleased
  done                Mark an in-progress goal completed
  fail                Mark an in-progress goal failed
  cancel              Cancel a queued, in-progress, or paused goal
  help                Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --config <PATH>  Config file to load instead of the default user + project files
  -h, --help           Print help

          Runtime budget per fresh automatic segment, in seconds [default: 900]
      --goal-verifier-timeout-seconds <GOAL_VERIFIER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS>
          Runtime budget per automatic acceptance command, in seconds [default: 300]
      --goal-max-segments <GOAL_MAX_SEGMENTS>
          Maximum lifetime fresh segments for one goal [default: 6]
      --goal-max-failures <GOAL_MAX_FAILURES>
          Pause after this many consecutive verifier/runtime failures [default: 2]
      --goal-poll-millis <GOAL_POLL_MILLIS>

          Emit machine-readable JSON

          Profile, provider/model pair, or auto target for each fresh segment
      --workdir <PATH>
          Canonical workdir shared by verifier commands and runtime segments
      --sandbox <SANDBOX>
          Workspace permission for each fresh segment [default: write] [possible values: read-only, write, full]
      --overall-timeout-seconds <OVERALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS>
          Overall pursuit budget in seconds (1 through 86400) [default: 3600]
      --segment-timeout-seconds <SEGMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS>
          Runtime budget per fresh segment in seconds (1 through 3600) [default: 900]
      --verifier-timeout-seconds <VERIFIER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS>
          Runtime budget per acceptance command in seconds (1 through 300) [default: 300]
      --max-segments <MAX_SEGMENTS>
          Maximum fresh runtime segments (1 through 64) [default: 6]
      --max-failures <MAX_FAILURES>
          Pause after this many consecutive verifier/runtime failures (1 through 16) [default: 2]
      --worker <WORKER>
          Exact active lease holder; pursuit never runs without a lease
